catalog.summary: Slides that scroll one page at a time.

roleDescriptions.words: messages.roleDescription and messages.slideRoleDescription, so a screen reader says the role in the page's own language

wiring.root: aria-label or aria-labelledby from the consumer; the name never repeats the word the role description already says
wiring.slide: aria-label from messages.slide unless the consumer names it
wiring.indicator: aria-selected on the current page, aria-controls names the first slide of the page
wiring.counter: aria-hidden, because the slide names and the announcement already carry the position

rotation.timer: the current indicator fills over the delay and freezes while the rotation pauses

ends.reason: a disabled button drops the focus it holds onto the body; the control stays focusable and does nothing

inView.peekPress: a press on a slide out of view reaches the viewport, which asks for that slide's page with reason pointer

announcement.when: a page change the reader asked for; never during the rotation

loop.behavior: next on the last page asks for the first, previous on the first asks for the last; the scroll travels back across the track

pages.source: the slides' own boxes in the viewport, so a container query that changes how many fit changes the pages
pages.slidesPerMove: a number, or page for the slides wholly in view

keyboard.effect: next page in a horizontal carousel, mirrored to previous in a right-to-left one
previous page in a horizontal carousel, mirrored to next in a right-to-left one
next page in a vertical carousel, nothing in a horizontal one so the page keeps scrolling
previous page in a vertical carousel, nothing in a horizontal one
moves focus into the slide picker
keyboard.focus: the current page's indicator, the only one in the tab sequence

keyboard.effect: next indicator, and its page, with no wrap at the end; mirrored in right-to-left
previous indicator, and its page, with no wrap at the start; mirrored in right-to-left
activates the rotation, previous or next control
keyboard.focus: stays on the control, so it can be pressed again

keyboard.effect: activates the rotation, previous or next control

motion.scroll: a critically damped spring, stiffness 8 over --_scroll-duration (the theme's long duration), launched at the speed the scroller already has; a request for the page already in flight keeps the flight
motion.reducedMotion: the duration collapses and the scroll lands at once

indicators.adaptive: past eight pages, dots more than two steps away shrink and those outside the window collapse; every one stays in the arrow ring

pointer.mouseDrag: draggable, from a threshold of four pixels along the axis; the click after a drag is cancelled
pointer.touch: the platform's own scroll, with snap
pointer.fadeSwipe: a swipe of forty pixels in fade asks for the neighbour page
pointer.release: one page in the way the hand moves when the release speed passes 0.25 px/ms, otherwise the page the release speed coasts to in 200 ms; never more than one page from where the drag began; the spring sets off at the release speed
pointer.edges: past an end the slides follow the pointer less and less (rubber band, constant 0.55 of the viewport) and spring back on release

clones.reason: a cloned slide duplicates the consumer's ids, focus targets, form controls and component state, and makes the index a fiction; the loop travels back instead

marquee.reason: a continuous ticker is motion with no state and no action, which the rubric refuses; a consumer composes it from a translate animation over duplicated content marked aria-hidden

wheelGestures.reason: a trackpad already scrolls the inline axis natively; a vertical mouse wheel is the page's, and taking it would trap the reader inside the carousel

scrollButtonPseudoElements.reason: ::scroll-button() and ::scroll-marker ship in Chromium alone, and their names come from CSS content, which no message provider reaches

familyAttributes.data-playing: root, while the rotation is on
familyAttributes.data-paused: root, while hover or a hidden document holds the rotation
familyAttributes.data-inview: slide, while half of it or more is in the viewport
familyAttributes.data-snap: slide, when a page starts at it
familyAttributes.data-measured: root, once the pages have been read from the layout
familyAttributes.data-moving: viewport, while the engine moves the scroll or a mouse drags it; written in the same task as the movement
